newsitem.title: CANADA: Crystallex stock gains on Venezuela hopes.
newsitem.headline: Crystallex stock gains on Venezuela hopes.

text.p: Crystallex International Corp shares soared further on Tuesday amid speculation that the company would succeed in gaining title to most of Placer Dome Inc's Las Cristinas gold property in Venezuela.
Crystallex stock was up 0.50 to 6.80 in Toronto after earlier hitting a new 52-week high of 7.35. That came after a 1.20 gain on Monday.
Placer was down 0.35 to 23.75 in Toronto.

Analysts said a recent appearance by Crystallex at a New York gold stock conference and a flurry of rumors were fueling investor hopes that Crystallex would prevail. Crystallex has been pressing its claims to Las Cristinas for months but Placer Dome contends they are totally unfounded.
A Crystallex spokesman was unavailable for comment. Sources said rumors swirled that Crystallex was negotiating with Placer to resolve the dispute and that Placer had made a rich offer to Crystallex.
Placer spokesman Hugh Leggatt said the talk was "preposterous." "All their claims are totally without foundation."

Whalen Beliveau analyst Dorothy Atkinson said she expected a new ruling soon from Venezuela's Supreme Court that would advance Crystallex's drive to gain title to the Las Cristinas blocks. "It does look as though ownership may well transfer to Crystallex," she said.
Crystallex has laid claim to two of the richest blocks at Las Cristinas and has said Venezuela's Supreme Court has ruled in its favor.

Placer vehemently denied this contention. "We are still the recognized owner. Nothing has changed," Leggatt said. Reports from Caracas have said that the Venezuelan Supreme Court has published Crystallex's claim but has not made a decision on the dispute.

Placer also denied Crystallex's claim that a Supreme Court ruling confirming its position had been gazetted in Venezuela. "Nothing has been gazetted. There has been no decree or announcement," Leggatt said.
But the dispute with Crystallex has clouded prospects for development of Las Cristinas.

Placer, which has 70 percent of the property and Venezuela's state-owned CVG the rest, had planned to begin construction on a US$576 million mine there last month. But it put that off until Venezuela eliminated doubts about Crystallex's claims and other final hurdles were cleared.
CVG and Venezuelan mining officials have also said Crystallex has no right to the Las Cristinas concession.
